explanation: Crusoe names him after the day of the week he saved his life. Defoe's 1719 novel was first presented as Crusoe's own true account, 'written by himself'.

claims.text: In Robinson Crusoe, Crusoe names the man he rescues Friday.
Crusoe does not name him Sunday, Monday or Thursday.
Crusoe names him Friday after the day of the week on which he saved his life.
The first edition presented the book as Crusoe's own account, 'written by himself', without naming Defoe.
